liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Morning Dew hot; Morning Dew rivals the one from 7/19/89 [22][31]
- **Help On the Way** (2 reviews): Jerry's tune-up setting the tempo had fans near Phil's side guessing the coming song; Great Help>Slip>Franklin's, with MIDI at its finest [24][31]
- **Slipknot!** (2 reviews): Reviewer ranks this Slipknot as favorite among all later versions, as if the snake was desperate to escape; Long and far-out Slipknot with fantastic MIDI work [24][28]
- **Victim Or The Crime** (1 review): Victim was very well played, though reviewer hoped for Sailor/Saint after Franklin's [28]
- **I Need a Miracle** (1 other source): The space leading into I Need A Miracle is kept inside that track [1]
- Promised Land was accidentally cut from the master; a first-generation alternate audience dub was crossfaded in from the end of Bird Song [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd89-10-08 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd89-10-08 s1t02 Foolish Heart**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd89-10-08 s1t03 Walkin' Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd89-10-08 s1t04 Candyman**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd89-10-08 s1t05 Me & My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd89-10-08 s1t06 Big River**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd89-10-08 s1t07 Stagger Lee**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]
- **gd89-10-08 s1t08 Queen Jane Approximately**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]

## The recordings

- **gd1989-10-08.142509.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 157 min [1]
- **gd89-10-08.sbd.unknown.8365.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 153 min; rated 4.62/5 by 26 [3]. Said about its sound: Reviewer complains the track splits on this soundboard are poor [29]
- **gd1989-10-08.sbd.carr.17732.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 153 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]. Said about its sound: Some analog generations seem present in the lineage, but artifacts are minimal [4]
- **gd1989-10-08.nak304.carpenter.89508.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 150 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [5]
- **gd1989-10-08.sbd.hinko.32427.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 152 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [6]
- **gd89-10-08.fob-schoeps.nawrocki.439.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 157 min; rated 4.86/5 by 7 [13]. Said about its sound: Front-of-board recording that puts you in the room; has a small cut in Me and My Uncle [28]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says everyone in the Hampton Coliseum sensed they were part of something special [20]
- Reviewer recalls a huge cheer when the house lights came up after the following night's show [20]
- Billed as the Warlocks, with the show only announced a few days beforehand [21]
- Rumor from soundcheck: Dark Star and Saint Stephen were chosen; crowds outside were thinner [21]
- Billed as Formerly The Warlocks, after the band was banned from Hampton Coliseum following fan incidents [33]
- Dark Star did appear in the next night's set, but Saint Stephen never came [21]
- Second set is weaker than its setlist suggests, despite Help on the Way into Slipknot returning [22]
- Show is often overshadowed by the following night's Dark Star, though energy from band and crowd was high [24]
- Next night gets the hype, but this show ranks among the year's best, maybe the 80s [31]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1989-10-08.142509.fob.schoeps.cmc4.mk4.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Ted Mattes' Master (FOB)Audience Dat; Schoeps CMC4/MK4 mics @ 110 degrees, ORTF, Schoeps t-bar stand, shoulder height > Monster… [1]
- **gd89-10-08.sbd.unknown.8365.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> Master Cass>DAT>CD [3]
- **gd1989-10-08.sbd.carr.17732.shnf**: transferred by Dan Carr; source: Soundboard [4]. Also: Dan Carr converted it to SHN with EAC on 12/10/01 [4]
- **gd1989-10-08.nak304.carpenter.89508.flac16**: taped by Ted Carpenter; transferred by Andrew F.; source: Nakamichi CM300's w/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's, with no Dolby. Mics on stand on the floor, near the soundboard [5]. Also: Second-set patch from ShnID-439 covers Drums at 8:14 through Space at 4:20 [5]
- **gd1989-10-08.sbd.hinko.32427.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Darryl Hinko; source: SBD > MC > DAT > CD > EAC > FLAC [6]. Also: Front-of-board Schoeps CMC34 microphones recorded to a Panasonic SV-250; Patches crossfaded into Space and We Bid You Goodnight from alternate sources [6]
- **gd89-10-08.fob-schoeps.nawrocki.439.sbeok.shnf**: source: Schoeps CMC34's -> Panasonic SV-250 [13]

## Art and photos

- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 10/8/89 Hampton Coliseum, Hampton, VA Disc…](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/27330686206/) [39]

Rumor from soundcheck: Dark Star and Saint Stephen were chosen; crowds outside were thinner
Dark Star did appear in the next night's set, but Saint Stephen never came
Second set is weaker than its setlist suggests, despite Help on the Way into Slipknot returning
Reviewer calls the Morning Dew hot
Jerry's tune-up setting the tempo had fans near Phil's side guessing the coming song
Reviewer ranks this Slipknot as favorite among all later versions, as if the snake was desperate to escape
Show is often overshadowed by the following night's Dark Star, though energy from band and crowd was high
Front-of-board recording that puts you in the room; has a small cut in Me and My Uncle
Long and far-out Slipknot with fantastic MIDI work
Victim was very well played, though reviewer hoped for Sailor/Saint after Franklin's
Reviewer complains the track splits on this soundboard are poor
Morning Dew rivals the one from 7/19/89
Great Help>Slip>Franklin's, with MIDI at its finest
Next night gets the hype, but this show ranks among the year's best, maybe the 80s
Master DAT recording by Ted Mattes; Charlie Miller made the transfer; front-of-board Schoeps CMC4 microphones
The space leading into I Need A Miracle is kept inside that track
Some analog generations seem present in the lineage, but artifacts are minimal
Dan Carr converted it to SHN with EAC on 12/10/01
Promised Land was accidentally cut from the master; a first-generation alternate audience dub was crossfaded in from the end of Bird Song
Second-set patch from ShnID-439 covers Drums at 8:14 through Space at 4:20
Front-of-board Schoeps CMC34 microphones recorded to a Panasonic SV-250
Patches crossfaded into Space and We Bid You Goodnight from alternate sources
